files.source/main.brs:
sub Main()
    screen = CreateObject("roSGScreen")
    port = CreateObject("roMessagePort")
    screen.setMessagePort(port)
    scene = screen.CreateScene("MainScene")
    screen.show()
    while true
        msg = wait(0, port)
        if type(msg) = "roSGScreenEvent" and msg.isScreenClosed() then return
    end while
end sub

declared.package: rm -f build/app.zip && mkdir -p build images && zip -qr build/app.zip manifest source components images -x '*.DS_Store'
declared.rules: A Roku channel written in BrightScript with SceneGraph. source/main.brs creates an roSGScreen and the MainScene; the UI lives in components/*.xml (SceneGraph nodes: Rectangle, Label, Poster, Group, LayoutGroup, Timer, Video, Audio, etc.) with their logic in .brs files they include via <script uri>. The screen is 1920x1080 (ui_resolutions=fhd); keep content inside a 5% safe margin, text at least 28px, a dark background. Input arrives in the focused component's onKeyEvent(key, press) with key names up, down, left, right, OK, back, play, rewind, fastforward, options, replay; return true when handled; returning false for back on the main scene exits the channel. A Keyboard or MiniKeyboard node takes typed text. Use a Timer node (repeat=true, observe its fire field) for animation or game loops, never a busy loop in a component. The render thread can't reach the network: every request of the app's own (roUrlTransfer for a feed or an API) runs in a Task node, a component of its own that extends Task, with interface fields for what it's asked and what it found, functionName set in init and control = "RUN" to start it; the scene observes the result field. A live connection runs in a Task too: on Roku OS 16 and later roWebSocket, and for server-sent events an roStreamSocket on which the Task writes the GET itself and reads the event lines as they arrive (roUrlTransfer answers only once a request is complete); check the version with roDeviceInfo's GetOSVersion() and fall back to asking again on a Timer. Saved data goes through Lamp's LampStore, never roRegistrySection directly: Roku keeps about 32 KB of saved data per channel, shared by every app Lamp puts on that Roku, so keep it small. BrightScript is case-insensitive, has no classes (use associative arrays), arrays are roArray, integer division uses \, and every component runs in its own scope (share state through m and node fields). print writes to the debug log. Pictures go in images/ and are referenced as pkg:/images/name.png. The manifest names the icon and splash pictures Lamp draws in images/ (mm_icon_focus_hd, mm_icon_focus_fhd, splash_screen_sd, splash_screen_hd, splash_screen_fhd, at icon_focus_hd.png, icon_focus_fhd.png, splash_sd.png, splash_hd.png and splash_fhd.png): keep those lines, add them when they're missing, and never draw or replace those files. A screensaver is an app of its own: its manifest adds screensaver_title={{NAME}} and source/main.brs a sub RunScreenSaver() that shows its scene the way Main does (keep Main, so it can be opened and tried); the person picks it under Settings, Theme, Screensaver. Keep it slow and dark, and move what it shows now and then. Lamp's support library is in components/Lamp and is packaged with the app.
